tenancy.honestTitle: What this page is not claiming
tenancy.honestBody: While the flag is off every model reports "Scope registered: No". That is the point: the disabled path registers nothing, so the compiled SQL is unchanged. The proof is a committed baseline captured before any tenancy code existed.
tenancy.auditBody: Run the audit. It refuses readiness while any row still has a null tenant, because those rows would disappear for everyone but a super-admin.
tenancy.failClosedBody: When scoping is active and no tenant resolves, the predicate becomes 1 = 0. No tenant means no rows, never all rows.

ladder.title: Precedence
ladder.description: Three rungs, evaluated top to bottom. The first one that matches wins — nothing is ever merged.

personal.label: Your layout
personal.body: A personal layout wins unconditionally, including one where every widget is hidden. Hiding everything is a deliberate choice, not an empty state.

role.label: Role default
role.body: With no personal layout, the default authored for the highest-priority role the user holds is shown. There is nothing to reset, so no reset control appears.

none.label: Nothing configured
none.body: No personal layout and no role default means the dashboard renders exactly as it did before this feature existed. No badge, no reset, no flag.

chain.title: Resolution chain
chain.description: One entry point, evaluated on every request. Nothing in it is cached, so losing or disabling a role corrects itself on the next page load.
chain.caption: The steps a dashboard layout is resolved through, and the result of each.

key.label: Key gate
key.result: The dashboard key is a closed set and is never taken from a request. An unknown key resolves to nothing.

guest.label: No user
guest.result: Nothing to resolve against, so nothing is returned.

personal.label: Personal row
personal.result: Found, so it wins. The source is reported as personal and the reset control appears.

role.label: Role default
role.result: One indexed query joins the role assignments, ordered by role priority. The first row found wins.

none.label: Nothing
none.result: The layout is null and the dashboard falls back to its declared order.

priority.title: Holding several roles
priority.description: Roles carry an admin-orderable priority. A user holding several gets the dashboard of their highest-priority role that has one. Predictable, never merged.
priority.fallThrough: A role without a dashboard is invisible to the ordering, so the next role down supplies one. A user is never blanked by their top role's silence.
priority.tie: Two roles sharing a priority are separated by role id, ascending — deterministic on every database, never left to assignment order.
priority.revocation: Deactivating a role, deleting it, or unassigning it takes effect on the very next request. A personal layout survives all three, because it carries no role provenance.

security.title: Two facts that hold at render time
security.instances: A role dashboard is authored by one person and rendered for another, so the stored payload is untrusted input. Every widget instance is re-derived against the VIEWING user's abilities on every render — an admin who drops a revenue widget into the viewer dashboard produces exactly zero instances for a viewer.
security.entries: Entries are filtered the same way. A widget key the viewer may not see never reaches their browser, so the payload cannot become an enumeration oracle for tiles they are not entitled to.

starters.title: Starter dashboards
starters.description: Sensible opening arrangements for the five built-in roles. Ordering only — every widget named here is something that role could already see.
starters.caption: Starter dashboard contents for each built-in role.
starters.note: Hiding here is tidying, not access control. Nothing in a starter grants, resurrects or discloses anything, and every widget is still re-filtered for the viewing user.
starters.optIn: The seeder is never wired into the database seeder and never runs on an upgrade. Run it explicitly, and re-run it safely — an existing role dashboard is never overwritten.

first.question: What happens to my current homepage?
first.answer: Nothing. The existing settings stay on disk and are converted into an equivalent block list you can review before saving.

second.question: How do I roll back?
second.answer: Empty the block list. The classic settings were never modified, so the old page returns exactly as it was.
